concept: localbench top-40 union KL estimator versus .kld full-vocab KLD
summary: Requests go to `/v1/completions` with `echo: true` and `logprobs: 40`, which returns top-40 logprobs for every prompt token.

facts.text: Requests go to `/v1/completions` with `echo: true` and `logprobs: 40`, which returns top-40 logprobs for every prompt token.
The chat template comes from the official model release, not GGUF metadata, and is the same for every quant of a model; prompts are rendered through `/v1/internal/chat-prompt`.
The author justifies top-40 as covering "virtually all the probability mass" with negligible approximation error; no measurement is given.
Per-token KL is averaged over all tokens and prompts for the headline number; top-1 agreement is the share of tokens where both models' argmax match.
The inference stack is TextGen with a patched llama.cpp fork that returns prompt logprobs.
Missing tokens use a floor, so the two truncated distributions need not sum to 1 over the union; whether the author renormalises is not stated.
13 Apr 2026: methodology post; the 7 Apr Gemma 4 31B post and the 25 Apr Qwen 3.6 27B post link to it as their full methodology.
Values run higher than Wikipedia-based KLD because inputs reach about 30k tokens across six task types; Q4_K_M numbers of 0.01-0.03 elsewhere are not comparable.

An estimator with a "min minus 2" floor penalises a quant that moves mass into tokens the reference ranks below 40 differently from a full-vocabulary sum, so ranking can differ in the tail even when means agree.
The patched llama.cpp is a fork, so a mainline build cannot reproduce the numbers without the patch.
localbench: top-40 error is negligible. The existing clamp dossier: the two estimators are different and absolute values are not interchangeable. Neither has a head-to-head measurement.
A reader asked on 16 Apr 2026 whether the harness or dataset is downloadable; the visible reply is not shown in the cached page.
localbench requests top-40 prompt logprobs via `/v1/completions` with `echo: true`.
localbench uses the official release's Jinja2 template for every quant, not the GGUF's embedded template.
localbench's top-1 agreement is the fraction of positions where quant and reference pick the same most likely token.
localbench does not publish a measured error bound for the top-40 truncation.
